_meta: A small curated glossary of Trithemius's technical Latin terms for the parallel-viewer hover glossary. Common words (omnium, autem, etc.) are deliberately omitted; this focuses on cipher/magic/technical vocabulary.

steganographia.en: covered writing — the art of hidden/occult correspondence
steganographia.note: From Greek στεγανός (covered) + γραφή (writing). The work's title.

polygraphia.en: many-writing — the art of writing in many ways

clavis.note: Title of two companion keys to the Steganographia and Polygraphia.

modus.note: Each Polygraphia book presents a distinct modus.

recta.note: In 'tabula recta', the canonical polyalphabetic grid.

alphabetum.note: Plural alphabeti. Each column in a Polygraphia table is one alphabetum.

salutatio.note: The Ave Maria cipher disguises letters as pious salutations.

terms.nuncupatio: the calling upon / naming (of a spirit)

numerus.note: The 'order of numerical letters' assigns each a code.

litera.note: Plural literae. Trithemius's 24-letter alphabet omits j.

subiectio.note: Mapping one letter or number under another.

terms.figur: a figure — a tabular or diagrammatic cipher form

coniuratio.note: The Steganographia's spirit operations open with one.

spiritus.note: The Steganographia operates through planetary/cardinæ spirits.

princeps.note: Plural principes. Each wind-direction has one.

dux.en: a duke — a spirit rank beneath a prince
dux.note: Plural duces. Day- and night-dukes serve each prince.

comes.en: a count / companion — a spirit rank

minister.note: Lower-ranking spirits subordinate to the dukes.

oriens.note: Also the name of the eastern spirit-quarter.

ars.note: ars steganographiae = the art of covered writing.

liber.note: Plural libri. The Polygraphia has six.

secundum.note: e.g. secundum ordinem = according to the order.

nigromantia.note: What Trithemius's critics accused the Steganographia of being.

cabala.note: Trithemius cites cabalistic number-operations in Book VI.

exemplum.note: Trithemius illustrates each modus with one.

vulgaris.note: scriptura vulgaris = plain writing, opposed to cipher.
